s1.syndrome_frame: Severe fatigue and muscular weakness with a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger, hypercalcemia, and multiple bone lesions
salient_findings: Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Patient is cachectic
Tumor on the right fourth finger has gradually enlarged in recent months
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance

shortlist.label: Brown tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology of finger tumor shows fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells, consistent with brown tumor, a known complication of hyperparathyroidism

shortlist.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum parathyroid hormone, hypercalcemia, and hypophosphatemia are consistent with primary hyperparathyroidism, which is also supported by the patient's history

shortlist.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a tumor on the right fourth finger and multiple bone lesions, in combination with primary hyperparathyroidism, suggests a possible diagnosis of hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome

shortlist.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
shortlist.why_kept: Radiography and CT scans show multiple bone lesions and resorption, consistent with osteitis fibrosa cystica, a complication of hyperparathyroidism

shortlist.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The severe hyperparathyroidism and multiple bone lesions, in combination with a nodule in the right thyroid lobe, raise the possibility of parathyroid carcinoma
